title: Unit – 2 : Session – 12 : SLO – 1  |  Implementation of Doubly Linked Lists — Concepts I
sections: A doubly linked list node typically contains data, a pointer to the next node, and a pointer to the PREVIOUS node.
The structure of a doubly linked list node in C often uses the keyword STRUCT.
In C, to create a node dynamically, we use the function MALLOC().
The first node of a doubly linked list is called the HEAD (START).
To insert a node at the beginning, the new node's next pointer should point to the OLD HEAD (first) node.
When inserting at the beginning, the previous pointer of the old head should point to the NEW node.
To insert a node at the end, we must traverse the list until we find the node whose next is NULL.
While inserting at the end, the new node's previous pointer should point to the LAST (current tail) node.
To delete the first node, we move the head pointer to the SECOND (next) node.
When deleting the first node, the new head's previous pointer must be set to NULL.
